reply.text:
Let me take a look at how your training has actually been going. Slumps happen to everyone, and you don't need to be at full motivation to get going again. We start from today.

I can't see any training, program or goals logged yet, so I'm working from scratch with you. Three things tend to help:

1. Shrink the bar. Aim for a short session you can't talk yourself out of, like 20 to 30 minutes, and count showing up as the win.
2. Pick a fixed time. Two or three set days beat "whenever I feel like it", because motivation usually follows the first few minutes of moving rather than arriving before them.
3. Give yourself a target. A specific goal, like a lift number or a distance, makes it easier to want to walk in the door.

If you'd like, I can build you a short, easy-to-start session for today, or a simple program around the days you can realistically train. Which sounds better, and what's been getting in the way lately: time, energy, or just boredom with the routine?
